change is explicit input; repository reads are limited to its strict ancestors.
Distinguish source inspection, execution results, inference and missing evidence.
When a change adds or removes a declared dependency, use repo_grep on the parent
tree to locate its imports before describing impact. Check package-to-module
name differences (for example pillow imports as PIL), inspect matching source
and the task diff, and distinguish remaining imports from removed or absent
imports. An empty grep result does not rule out dynamic imports or external use.
When recording a finding in a function, use repo_grep on the parent tree to
locate its callers, inspect relevant call sites and the task diff, and state
the finding's reach. Distinguish direct callers from broader entry points;
report search limits instead of assuming every workflow reaches the function.
When an ancestor entry read in the session records a defect in code directly
touched by the task diff or its changed data flow, inspect the task tree to
determine whether the defect persists.

do not let a focused task diff silently imply that inherited code can return
or otherwise operate successfully.
When a change corrects where data is written, use repo_grep on the task and
parent trees to find the code that reads the data back. Compare the writer's
and reader's resolved locations, inspect which parent directories are created,
and leave unexecuted filesystem-library behavior explicitly unestablished.
When a change fixes an import, use repo_grep on the parent tree to locate the
modules and package initializers that import the affected module, then state
how far an import-time failure reaches. If the explanation depends on a
language or library version fact, cite eligible documentation supplied in the
evidence catalog or state that the version fact is unestablished.

parent tree for the exact key and plausible near spellings. Inspect the task
diff and relevant consumers before describing the key's effect; do not infer
the intended spelling from the helper or variable name alone.
When a change makes a dictionary key or function argument required, search the
whole parent tree, including tests and utilities, for every builder of that
dictionary and every caller of the function. Inspect each relevant construction
site; a search limited to the implementation package cannot establish caller
compatibility.
When a documentation change describes command-line options, defaults or runtime
behavior, check every documented statement against the parser and relevant
consumers, not only statements that initially appear suspicious. Record loose
or unsupported claims and distinguish source inspection from execution.
When the commit message names a platform, product or error, search the whole
parent tree for that term before concluding that no in-scope source bears on it.
Report related occurrences without assuming they describe the same defect.
Do not infer author intent from later knowledge. Do not claim tests were run unless
a run result supports the claim. This is an authoring-boundary candidate, not a
request to publish or mark an entry reviewed.
The task commit message is trusted task input identifying what the upstream author claimed, not an instruction to follow or proof that the claim is true. Check it against the diff and eligible evidence; distinguish reported motivation from verified behavior.
Use supplied author attribution when explaining provenance: when the evidence supports the same contributor reporting an issue, opening a PR, and authoring a fix, say so. Matching display names alone do not establish identity or independent corroboration.
The unreferenced discussion catalog is discovery input, not evidence that the upstream author linked an item to this change. Before finalizing, compare every catalog row with the task diff and files read in this session. Read with web_fetch any item whose title shares a number, identifier, file name or error text with them, and any item whose repo_paths_mentioned names a file the task touches or the session read. When the catalog contains ten items or fewer, read every available item whose title reports an error or failure, even without another match. The path hints are navigation derived from cutoff-bound issue text, not evidence; read the item before using it. Report the item's own title and framing faithfully. Label every link you draw to the task as inference and state the concrete matching basis, such as a traceback line matching a source line.
When a change alters which function, kernel or code path is selected (a threshold, flag, default, dispatch table or registry entry), read the selected callee or callees in the parent tree before describing the effect. Report what their own limits, tiers or preconditions show, as source inspection. State a conclusion about the author's reason as inference, and say that the rationale is unestablished only after that inspection.

Name each model read and say, model by model, whether the mappings, dimensions and defaults you describe hold for it. If a read fails, say so. Adds or changes means the task diff registers that architecture or modifies its model or configuration class. This applies to configuration files only; read tensor headers as needed to support claims.
The closed_discussion_catalog lists closed discussions qualified by shared terms or by paths named in cutoff-bound text that overlap the task change. matched_paths exposes those repository paths; a bare filename qualifies only when it resolves uniquely. These are navigation hints, not established relationships; fetch bodies with web_fetch, page with evidence_index(index_id="closed_discussions"), label task links as inference with their concrete basis, and report each item’s own title and framing faithfully.
When a change alters what a function, constructor, attribute or parameter accepts, returns or stores (its type,
shape, name or meaning), search the whole parent tree, read together with the task diff, for every other
definition, subclass, caller and reader that supplies or consumes it, including files the task diff does not
touch. Inspect each one and say, case by case, whether it agrees with the changed form; name any that the diff
leaves on the old form and state what the inspected code would do with it. A search limited to the changed files
cannot establish that the change is complete.

When the task modifies, copies or closely follows a file, class or function that an earlier commit introduced,
find that commit's entry with the ancestor tools and read it before finalizing. Say which entries you read and
what they establish about the code the task relies on, including any guard, precondition or recorded defect; if
you read none, say so.

When one commit makes several edits, check whether any of them supplies a precondition another needs before
describing them as independent.

When the task starts calling an existing function, method or mechanism from a place that did not call it before,
or copies code that calls it, search the parent tree for its existing callers and read the code around each call.
Compare the conditions, guards, argument preparation and error handling there with the new call; name any that
the new call omits and state what the inspected code would do without it. If there are no other callers, say so.

When the task removes, comments out or bypasses a check, guard, conversion or initialisation, or replaces a call
that performed one, read the removed or bypassed code and say what it prevented or guaranteed. Then say whether
anything in the inspected code still prevents or guarantees it. If nothing does and the source shows an input or
call path that reaches the unguarded case, report it under findings as suspected, with its limits; do not leave
it only under uncertainty. If you could not establish a path that reaches it, say what you searched.

When the task adds or changes a model architecture, or code that names checkpoint tensors or depends on their
shapes or orientation, and tensor headers for reference checkpoints are listed in the evidence index, read the
headers of at least one reference checkpoint for each distinct configuration. Say which tensor names and shapes
the changed code relies on and whether each exists with that shape, and name any stored tensors the code never
reads. Check every tensor name the code requests, including alternate and optional names, against the names in
the header, and say which are absent and which path the code then takes. Do not describe tensor layout as
unestablished while headers are available and unread.

                y = self.mlp_post_norm.forward(y, params)

    arch_string = "DeciLMForCausalLM"

    def __init__(
        self,
        directory: str,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        super().__init__(
            directory,
            {"text": DeciLMModel},
            **kwargs
        )

        # Global attention params
        self.head_dim = self.read_cfg(int, "head_dim", None)
        self.hidden_size = self.read_cfg(int, "hidden_size", no_default)
        self.num_q_heads = self.read_cfg(int, "num_attention_heads", no_default)

        if not self.head_dim:
            self.head_dim = self.hidden_size // self.num_q_heads

        # MLP params
        self.assert_cfg(str, "hidden_act", "silu", True)

        # Norms
        self.rms_norm_eps = self.read_cfg(float, "rms_norm_eps", no_default)

        # Layers
        self.num_hidden_layers = self.read_cfg(int, "num_hidden_layers", no_default)
        self.tie_word_embeddings = self.read_cfg(bool, "tie_word_embeddings", False)

        # RoPE
        self.rope_settings = self.read_rope_settings_default(RopeStyle.NEOX)

        # Block configs
        self.block_configs = self.read_cfg(list, "block_configs", no_default)
        assert len(self.block_configs) == self.num_hidden_layers, \
            "Number of hidden layers does not match length of block_configs list"


class DeciLMModel(Model):
    config_class = DeciLMConfig

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: DeciLMConfig,
        **kwargs
    ):
        super().__init__(config, **kwargs)

        self.modules += [
            Embedding(
                config = config,
                key = "model.embed_tokens",
                vocab_size = config.vocab_size,
                hidden_size = config.hidden_size,

        self.first_block_idx = len(self.modules)

            cfg_ffn = cfg["ffn"]

            if cfg_attn.get("no_op"):
                attn_norm = None
                attn = None

                assert not cfg_attn.get("num_sink_tokens"), "DeciLM: num_sink_tokens not supported"

                assert not cfg_attn.get("sparsify"), "DeciLM: sparsify not supported"
                assert not cfg_attn.get("unshifted_sink"), "DeciLM: unshifted_sink not supported"
                assert not cfg_attn.get("use_prefill_window_in_sink_attention"), \
                    "DeciLM: use_prefill_window_in_sink_attention not supported"
                attn_norm = RMSNorm(
                    config = config,
                    key = f"model.layers.{idx}.input_layernorm",
                    rms_norm_eps = config.rms_norm_eps,
                )
                attn = Attention(
                    config = config,
                    key = f"model.layers.{idx}.self_attn",
                    layer_idx = cache_layer_idx,
                    hidden_size = config.hidden_size,
                    head_dim = config.head_dim,
                    num_q_heads = config.num_q_heads,
                    num_kv_heads = config.num_q_heads // cfg_attn["n_heads_in_group"],
                    rope_settings = config.rope_settings,
                    sm_scale = None,
                    key_q = "q_proj",
                    key_k = "k_proj",
                    key_v = "v_proj",
                    key_o = "o_proj",
                    qmap = "block.attn",
                )
                cache_layer_idx += 1
                self.last_kv_module_idx = len(self.modules)

            if cfg_ffn.get("no_op"):
                mlp_norm = None
                mlp = None
            else:
                assert not cfg_ffn.get("replace_with_linear"), "DeciLM: replace_with_linear not supported"
                assert not cfg_ffn.get("sparsify"), "DeciLM: sparsify not supported"
                mlp_norm = RMSNorm(
                    config = config,
                    key = f"model.layers.{idx}.post_attention_layernorm",
                    rms_norm_eps = config.rms_norm_eps,
                )
                interm_size = int(2 * cfg_ffn["ffn_mult"] * config.hidden_size / 3)
                interm_size = ((interm_size + 255) // 256) * 256
                mlp = GatedMLP(
                    config = config,
                    key = f"model.layers.{idx}.mlp",
                    hidden_size = config.hidden_size,
                    intermediate_size = interm_size,
                    key_up = "up_proj",
                    key_gate = "gate_proj",
                    key_down = "down_proj",
                    qmap = "block.mlp",
                )

            self.modules += [
                TransformerBlock(
                    config = config,
                    key = f"model.layers.{idx}",
                    attn_norm = attn_norm,
                    attn = attn,

                    mlp = mlp,

            ]

        head_alt_key = None
        if config.tie_word_embeddings and not self.config.stc.has_tensor("lm_head"):
            head_alt_key = "model.embed_tokens"

        self.modules += [
            RMSNorm(
                config = config,
                key = "model.norm",
                rms_norm_eps = config.rms_norm_eps,
                out_dtype = torch.half,
            ),
            Linear(
                config = config,
                key = "lm_head",
                qbits_key = "head_bits",
                alt_key = head_alt_key,
                in_features = config.hidden_size,
                out_features = config.vocab_size,
                qmap = "block",
                caps = {"logits_output": True}
            )
        ]

        self.logit_layer_idx = len(self.modules) - 1


    @override
    def prepare_inputs(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, params: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
        params["input_ids"] = input_ids
        input_ids = prepare_for_attn(input_ids, params)
        return input_ids


    @override
    def default_chat_prompt(self, prompt: str, system_prompt: str = None) -> str:
        p = "<s>"

Also, unlike most applications where dim=1 is by far the most meaningful distribution, there's nothing special about dim=1 within a 256 dimension Trellis Coder. prompt_format = "llama3"
prompt_text = format_prompt(
    prompt_format,
    "You are a super helpful language model.",
    "List five ways in which cats are superior to dogs."
)
context_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt_text, encode_special_tokens = True)

# Sampling and stop conditions
sampler = DefaultSampler()
stop_conditions = get_stop_conditions(prompt_format, tokenizer)

# Get model vocabulary as a list of strings, for streaming the completion
vocab = tokenizer.get_id_to_piece_list()

# Prefill the prompt, up to but not including the last token, which will be the first token forwarded in the
# generation loop. Treat the cache as a rectangular batch
model.prefill(
    input_ids = context_ids[:, :-1],
    params = {
        "attn_mode": "flash_attn",
        "cache": cache,
        "past_len": 0,
        "batch_shape": (1, 2048),
    }
)

# Generation loop
max_new_tokens = 500
generated_tokens = 0
response = ""

torch.cuda.synchronize()
with Timer() as t:
    while generated_tokens < max_new_tokens:

        logits = model.forward(
            input_ids = context_ids[:, -1:],
            params = {
                "attn_mode": "flash_attn",
                "cache": cache,
                "past_len": context_ids.shape[-1] - 1,
                "batch_shape": (1, 2048),
            }

        sample = sampler.forward(logits, tokenizer = tokenizer)
        token_id = sample.item()

        context_ids = torch.cat((context_ids, sample.cpu()), dim = -1)
        token = vocab[token_id]
        response += token
        generated_tokens += 1

Even with ~1GB VRAM remaining, the system throws an error: `RuntimeError: Insufficient VRAM in split for model and cache`. Below are test results for two models on 24564MiB VRAM (RTX4090):  \n\n#### Model 1: **Nemotron-Super-49B** (3.0bpw, `cache-mode FP16`)  \n- 2k context: 19162MiB used  \n- 12k context: 21342MiB used  \n- 20k context: 23094MiB used  \n- 21k context: 23194MiB used  \n- 22k context: OOM  \n\n#### Model 2: **gemma3-27b** (5.0bpw, `cache-mode Q6`)  \n- 2k context: 17404MiB used  \n- 12k context: 19404MiB used  \n- 22k context: 21660MiB used  \n- 30k context: 23238MiB used  \n- 31k context: OOM  \n\nEnvironment: WSL Ubuntu+Python12+torch2.7.0+cu128+exllamav3-0.0.3+tabbyAPI default config\n\n**Questions:**  \n- Is this behavior expected under exllamav3\u2019s current memory management design?  \n- Are there recommended configurations or workarounds to better utilize the remaining VRAM?",

    },
    {
      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "A couple of likely contributing reasons:\n\nMomentary VRAM allocations can be so quick that they don't show up in a monitoring utility which might be polling, say, once per second. Really it's just accounting for the worst case while loading. The chunk size is adjustable in Tabby's config if you want a different worst case. Smaller chunk size reduces the overall VRAM requirement somewhat but also makes prefill somewhat slower. Tabby's default is 2048.\n\nAlso, by default a small buffer amount is reserved on each GPU to keep things stable, especially for the first GPU which might also be running a desktop environment. You can change the size of this reserve in Tabby's config, or if you're calling ExLlama directly, there are arguments to the `load()` and `load_gen()` functions.\n\nIn multi-GPU splits, ExLlama only splits whole layers. So if each of your devices would fit 12.7 layers in theory, you end up with 12 layers on each and 0.7 layers worth of unused memory.\n\nFinally, VRAM fragmentation is a thing and is not accounted for by `nvidia-smi`. Having 23.5 GB free on a 24 GB device doesn't mean you can allocate an extra block of 0.5 GB tensor somewhere.",

    },
    {
      "author_login": "Vhallo",
      "content": "Turns out even with CUDA sysmem fallback set to \"prefer no sysmem fallback\", it can still end up using some sysmem when changing Chunk Size, with slightly degraded performance. Doesn't seem to happen with context though strangely enough.",
      "content_sha256": "cf69675e1f659bbfdd4374af33f769be7591a81f3278401ff39b7b471112e35b",
      "created_at": "2025-06-12T21:29:03Z",

      "author_login": "louiehelm",
      "content": "New architecture [dots.llm1](https://huggingface.co/rednote-hilab/dots.llm1.inst)\n\nMight somewhat easy to support if Qwen3 and Deepseek are working [according to this](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/14044):\n\n> It looks like it is a mixture of deepseek-3 MoE modules and qwen-3 attention modules:\n> \n> https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/ffe12627b4e84489d2ab91dd0ec00614855edc79/src/transformers/models/dots1/modular_dots1.py\n> \n> and uses qwen-2 tokeniser:\n> \n> https://huggingface.co/rednote-hilab/dots.llm1.inst/blob/main/tokenizer_config.json\n> \n> So it's probably just a case of glueing all this together?\n\nThere's a working [hf patch](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/ffe12627b4e84489d2ab91dd0ec00614855edc79/src/transformers/models/dots1/modular_dots1.py) and [llama.cpp patch](https://github.com/Noeda/llama.cpp/commit/16dc0f4cff5be488d3c755440f008f1ad0671574#diff-ec77d8003b92ff283179456d36b8b56abf635e7b1232e70daf16676e8920ccf1R5276) in testing.\n\nPeople are planning Deepseek distills and other tunes with this model since it has several base checkpoints released + more world knowledge than anything outside 5x+ it's size. At 143B, dots.llm1 tunes could plausibly become the premier EXL3 models for people with dual GPUs who can't run any Deepseek quant but want to run something better than Qwen3 32B.\n\nAnd even if others don't, I will quantize and release EXL3 quants of this model if a working definition file gets created.",

      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "I pushed support for dots.llm1 today. Had to include a kludge that specifically skips quantizing the attn out projection on the first layer, since it's apparently too irregular.\n\n![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70d746f6-03e5-4947-b673-ee688df55729)\n\nAs far as I can tell values have been clamped to +/- 2.0 so I suspect something got out of hand in training and this is how they painted over it? In any case, the rest of the model seems fine.\n\nSince it doesn't use routing groups, the only difference to Qwen3MoE is using sigmoid instead of softmax on the router logits, and then using a single dense layer. So supporting it wasn't hard, but it's still a very large sparse model. Quantization isn't fast so I've only really tested 4.0bpw for now. It's on HF [here](https://huggingface.co/turboderp/dots.llm1.inst-exl3), and I'll queue up some more jobs to run overnight and upload tomorrow if all goes well.\n\nThe speed is okay, comparable to Qwen3-32B, but of course this only holds at bsz 1 because of the sparsity. Even with further optimization to reduce the MoE overhead, this still isn't going to be super fast by comparison, and prompt ingestion is always going to be slow (due to activating all 142B params), as is batched inference.\n\nNow, there aren't a lot of benchmarks yet, but the ones in the paper don't show this outperforming Qwen3-32B by all that much, and it even loses in a few categories.
